text:
maya: Heads up — forecasts show a ~30% spike in spot GPU scarcity in us-west-2 starting tonight. If we don't change bidding we risk multiple evictions for long-running finetunes. Any thoughts on region-aware hedging + failover?

arjun: Do you have the traffic/capacity numbers? which instance families? SLOs we need to protect? :thinking:

maya: Mostly a100-80 and a100-40 pools for experiments + some gdx-p3 like batches. SLOs: training jobs are best-effort but prod inferences p99 must stay <200ms. Grafana link: (grafana/redwood/gpu-capacity) — spike shows us-west-2 spot fulfillment drop from 96% -> 58% in last 6h.

liam: Sounds like classic region-local blackout. My brain: 1) route critical inference to dedicated/different region 2) shift long-running to capacity-optimized pools (lower eviction) 3) keep cheap eval runs on price-optimized pools.

maya: Proposed quick policy below. Want feedback before we push a small rollout.

```yaml
bid_policy:
  - name: training-long
    families: [a100-80, a100-40]
    mode: capacity_optimized
    max_bid_pct: 0.9  # allow up to 90% of on-demand to avoid churn
    warm_buffer: 0.05  # 5% reserved on dedicated for hard SLOs

  - name: eval-short
    families: [g4dn, p3]
    mode: price_optimized
    max_bid_pct: 0.45

fallbacks:
  - region_failover: [us-east-1, eu-west-1]
  - hard_fallback: dedicated_pool
  - eviction_ttl: 60  # seconds to drain/ckpt
```

ron: eviction_ttl=60 ok but we must shorten checkpoint intervals for long jobs. I'd set ckpt every 5-10min and persist last-2 states so we can resume quickly. Also ensure autoscaler keeps a few prewarmed nodes for heavy models.

liam: Also consider cross-pool allocation weighting so we don't blast one pool with all requests. e.g. weights = {a100-80:0.6, a100-40:0.2, g4dn:0.2} and move weights dynamically by fulfillment rate.

arjun: Cost tradeoffs? pushing bid_pct up to 0.9 will hit budget. Any roughs?

maya: quick back-of-envelope: our baseline spot spend is ~$120k/mo for training. If we bump a subset to 0.9 on 30% of capacity, estimated delta ~$14k/mo but we expect eviction incidents to drop from ~7/month -> ~2/month, each incident costs ~3-6 hours of manual ops + lost work (~$5k/incident). So net better ROI.

ops-bot: automated: [alert] instance-eviction detected us-west-2 a100-40 x3 at 1769505601

maya: ops-bot event confirms timing. Rollout plan: 1) A/B test policy on 10% of batch jobs (non-prod) in us-west-2 for 24h, 2) monitor fulfillment, evictions, cost delta, 3) if fulfillment >85% and evictions down, ramp to 50%, else rollback.

ron: +1. Add a metric alert: if p99 latency for inference >200ms for 5m during test -> rollback immediately.

liam: I'll run allocator sim overnight. Command to reproduce locally: `./simulator/bin/run --policy policies/region-hedge.yaml --duration 24h --seed 42`

maya: Thanks — action items: liam run sim and share results by EOD, ron update checkpoint daemon to 5min default for test jobs, arjun I need a quick cost sign-off if delta >$20k/mo. We'll push the A/B flag to 10% after sim.

arjun: noted, I'll watch the cost channel and give final OK. :thumbsup:

maya: Cool. If sim looks good we'll flip the flag at 1800 UTC.

liam: copying a tiny pressure-test snippet to hammer spot pools: `hey -c 200 -z 1m https://deploy-test/allocate?family=a100-40` — we'll use that to validate fulfillment rates.

maya: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post results and the rollout toggle when ready. :rocket:
